content.user_title: Build Native Android Apps with Kotlin
content.value_statement: Android projects can fail from weak structure, inconsistent UI, and build issues. This skill gives direct Kotlin, Compose, Gradle, accessibility, and testing guidance.
actual_capabilities: Assess Android project structure and required Gradle files.
Guide Kotlin and Jetpack Compose implementation patterns.
Explain Material Design 3 layout, typography, color, and motion rules.
Support accessibility checks for labels, contrast, touch targets, and screen readers.
Recommend Android test layers, dependencies, and Gradle test commands.
Diagnose common build errors, dependency conflicts, and resource naming issues.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete generated application by itself.
It does not replace testing on real Android devices and emulator targets.
Version examples may need adjustment for each project dependency catalog.
It cannot verify Play Store compliance without project files and release context.

use_cases.title: Start a Native Android Project
use_cases.description: Plan the required Gradle files, module layout, AndroidX settings, and first debug build.

use_cases.title: Review Compose UI Quality
use_cases.description: Check screens against Material Design 3, adaptive layout, accessibility, and performance guidance.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Build and Test Workflows
use_cases.description: Resolve dependency conflicts, select test layers, and run appropriate Gradle validation commands.

prompt_templates.title: Assess My Android Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Android project structure. Identify missing Gradle, manifest, resource, and Kotlin files before implementation starts.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Compose Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Jetpack Compose screen plan for this feature. Include state handling, accessibility labels, spacing, typography, and error states.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Build Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Android build error and recent Gradle changes. Explain the likely cause and propose a minimal fix sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Test Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a layered Android test strategy for this feature. Separate unit, Robolectric, Compose UI, Espresso, and managed device coverage.

output_examples.input: Review a new Android app folder before coding begins.
output: Project assessment with missing Gradle, manifest, resource, and source files.
Recommended first build step and AndroidX configuration checks.
Warnings about wrapper setup and dependency version alignment.

output_examples.input: Improve a Compose checkout screen for quality and accessibility.
output: Screen review covering touch targets, contrast, state handling, and layout spacing.
Material Design 3 recommendations for buttons, text fields, and navigation.
Performance notes for recomposition, loading states, and error handling.

output_examples.input: Add tests for a ViewModel and a Compose user flow.
output: Test layer plan that separates JVM tests from device or emulator tests.
Dependency alignment notes for coroutines, Compose, Espresso, and AndroidX Test.
Suggested commands for local unit tests and instrumentation validation.

best_practices: Run a debug build before adding complex business logic.
Match dependency versions to the project catalog and existing Gradle files.
Review accessibility, performance, and adaptive layouts before release.
anti_patterns: Adding test dependencies without checking existing project versions.
Blocking the main thread with network, file, or database work.
Using reserved Android resource names that can cause build conflicts.

faq.question: Does this skill create a full Android app?
faq.answer: It guides setup, implementation, review, and troubleshooting. A complete app still depends on the project requirements.

faq.question: Does it support Jetpack Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Compose state, lifecycle, UI quality, testing, and common mistake guidance.

faq.question: Can it help with Gradle build errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides diagnosis steps for dependency conflicts, wrapper setup, resource errors, and stack traces.

faq.question: Does it cover Android accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers content descriptions, touch targets, contrast, screen readers, and accessible interaction patterns.

faq.question: Can it choose dependency versions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends checking the project version catalog and existing Gradle files before adding dependencies.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
